svg.title: A replay-safe SQL load with checked rollback
svg.desc: Transactional PostgreSQL proof using an invented fixture. One batch, three runs and four checkpoints are retained after a repeated full pipeline. Exact same batch ID and JSONB payload is a no-op. Eleven passing SQL notices were retained, including six rejected CALL cases: orphan checkpoint P0001; duplicate run ID 23505; late checkpoint failure 23514; duplicate checkpoint key 23505; changed replay payload P0001; invalid array shape P0001. Each rejection test verified that all three table counts matched their own pre-call counts; test-only rows were rolled back. Actual SQL CSV matched an independent Decimal calculation: r1 (100 minus 60) divided by 10 equals 4; r2 (100 minus 60) divided by 20 equals 2; r3 has zero budget and no checkpoints, retains initial loss 50, and returns NULL rather than a ratio. Source: public SQL proof retained PostgreSQL 18.6 execution dated 2026-10-01, tests.sql, synthetic.json and actual_summary.csv. Small synthetic AI-assisted demonstration, not throughput, concurrency or enterprise-scale evidence. PostgreSQL was not rerun to create the figure.
